summary: Praga Caput Regni is a dense action-drafting euro where players build up personal tableaus of city districts, cathedral levels, and university tracks by choosing actions on a shared central board. It's a heavy points-optimization puzzle with several interlocking scoring engines that reward planning a coherent long-term strategy over reacting turn to turn.
praised: Rich, interlocking systems that feel satisfying to optimize
High replayability from variable setup and multiple viable strategies
Elegant action-selection mechanism (the crane) that creates real decisions
criticised: Steep learning curve and rules overhead for new players
Can suffer from analysis paralysis given the many options
Thematic integration feels thin compared to the mechanical depth

interaction.kind: area majority and shared board competition
interaction.detail: Players compete for limited actions on the shared action crane and for area-majority bonuses on the map, so timing and racing for key spots matters, but most of the actual building happens on each player's own tableau. The shared elements (board spaces, majority bonuses) create indirect pressure rather than direct attacks.

scoring.why: Final score is a sum across many largely independent tracks and structures — favor/prestige track, cathedral windows, bridge, university, deeds, and scoring cards each contribute separately.
scoring.how_you_win: Use action-crane moves to build up the cathedral, bridge, and university, place workers and deeds around the city, and climb the favor track, then add up points from all these separate scoring elements at game end — highest total wins.

similar: Merv: The Heart of the Silk Road
